questions.question: What color are warning signs for hazardous locations?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow with black letters.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Always pay attention to these signs.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per alcoholic drink before riding, what may still happen?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side effects may still remain.
questions.explanation: Your body eliminates about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system and affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: When does alcohol impair your ability to ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: Well below the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol is unsafe. Impairment begins well below the legal limit.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How should you cross angled railroad tracks?

options.text: By proceeding straight within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: By proceeding straight within your lane.
questions.explanation: Go straight through your lane when crossing angled tracks. Turning to approach at a right angle can push you into another lane.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing on a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen day and night, so be visible at all times.

questions.question: What happens if you take a turn too fast?

options.text: It is acceptable as long as you stay under the speed limit.
It is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
It is acceptable as long as no vehicles are near you.
You may end up in another lane or leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may end up in another lane or leave the road.
questions.explanation: Taking turns too fast is dangerous. You could end up in another lane or off the road. Always slow down for turns.

questions.question: What does a plastic face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: How do you swerve on a motorcycle?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: Press the handgrip on the side you want to go. To go left, press the left handgrip, then press right to recover. To go right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, what is best?

options.text: Let one rider pass completely before the next rider begins to pass.
Let several riders pass at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no more motorcycles are coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let one rider pass completely before the next rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: In a group, pass one at a time. Each rider must finish passing and get back in formation before the next rider passes.

questions.question: When you ride a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank to help balance the motorcycle while turning. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handlebars.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle slowly.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes because they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Motorcycles are hard for other drivers to see at night. What should a motorcycle rider do?

options.text: Slow down when riding at night.
Sound the horn repeatedly when riding at night.
Stay directly in front of another vehicle to be seen in their headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when riding at night.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, slow down and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of the car ahead to help you see farther. Use your high beam headlight unless you are following or meeting another vehicle. Be flexible about your lane position.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery road, what should you do?

options.text: Lean into the slippery section to maintain balance.
Keep your speed steady to improve traction.
Do not worry about the road conditions.
Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as needed.
questions.explanation: It is best to avoid slippery roads entirely. If you must go through one, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. Choose a position that gives you the most space and helps other drivers see you better.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle slowly.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because this makes the wobble worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Do not use the brakes because they can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders ride?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front of the group. This allows experienced riders in the back to watch them.

questions.question: In New York, how long is a motorcycle registration valid?
questions.correctAnswerText: One year
questions.explanation: Most motor vehicle registrations in New York are for two years, but motorcycle registrations last only one year. They expire on April 30 each year.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be which of the following?
questions.correctAnswerText: A speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means to proceed carefully. Slow down and watch for hazards when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light.
